instrument: City of Riverbank urgency moratorium on data center entitlements
summary: The city council unanimously adopted a 45-day urgency moratorium on new land-use entitlements for data centers, effective immediately, to study water, energy, noise and land-use impacts. Staff recommended defining a data center as 5,000 square feet or more of server space or a designed electrical load of 3 MW or more. Riverbank has no code provision specifically authorizing or barring data centers; projects would proceed by conditional use permit.
notes: The city had been approached by five potential developers, including one proposing a project at the former Army Ammunitions Plant. Aemetis president Andy Foster spoke against the pause, describing a 60 MW facility with minimal local water use and dedicated power lines. Spartan Data Centers and Aemetis publicly announced the Riverbank Technology Center during the pause; as of late August the city reported no formal application on file. Derived: 45 days from September 8 runs to about October 23; California Government Code 65858 permits extension up to two years.
confidence_note: Relayed; the urgency ordinance has not been read. The expiry date is derived from the adoption date and has not been confirmed against the ordinance's effective date.

source.citation: Modesto Bee and local reporting, September 2026
